items.readable_text:
Content:
A one-step multiplication equation is an equation like
[MATH: 6x=15,]
where the variable is multiplied by a number.

Content:
To solve a one-step multiplication equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operation that is applied to it.

Content:
For example, in the equation above, the variable [MATH: x] is multiplied by [MATH: 6.] The opposite of multiplying by [MATH: 6] is dividing by [MATH: 6.]

Content:
So, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 6] and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: 6x|= 15; 6x ÷ 6|= 15 ÷ 6; (6 ÷ 6)x|= (15)/(6); 1x|= (15 ÷ 3)/(6 ÷ 3); x|= (5)/(2)]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution. Notice that the solution is a fraction. When solving multiplication equations, the answer may be a fraction, even if the initial equation only contains whole numbers.

Content:
Note: Dividing by the coefficient indeed removes it from the left-hand side. This is because dividing a product by a number is equivalent to dividing its coefficient:
[MATH: 6x \div 6 = (6 \div 6)x]

Content:
Recall that if the variable appears on the right-hand side (e.g., [MATH: 15=6x]), you may first swap the left and right sides of the equation to get [MATH: 6x=15.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
Sometimes, the coefficient of the variable in a multiplication equation is a fraction, such as in the equation

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}x=2.]

Content:
To isolate [MATH: x,] we need to undo multiplication by [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}.] We could do this by dividing both sides by [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}] as before.

Content:
However, dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, to solve a multiplication equation with a rational coefficient, we multiply both sides by the reciprocal of the coefficient.

Content:
In our case, the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}] is [MATH: \dfrac{5}{4}.] We multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: \dfrac{5}{4}] and simplify.

Content:
On the left-hand side, we can re-group the numbers to multiply the fractions first. On the right-hand side, we can multiply fractions by first swapping denominators:

Content:
[MATH: (4)/(5)x|= 2; (4)/(5)x × (5)/(4)|= 2 × (5)/(4); ((4)/(5) × (5)/(4))x|= (2)/(4) × (5)/(1); 1x|= (1)/(2) × (5)/(1); x|= (5)/(2)]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
A one-step multiplication equation is an equation like
[MATH: 6x=15,]
where the variable is multiplied by a number.

Content:
To solve a one-step multiplication equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operation that is applied to it.

Content:
For example, in the equation above, the variable [MATH: x] is multiplied by [MATH: 6.] The opposite of multiplying by [MATH: 6] is dividing by [MATH: 6.]

Content:
So, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 6] and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: 6x|= 15; 6x ÷ 6|= 15 ÷ 6; (6 ÷ 6)x|= (15)/(6); 1x|= (15 ÷ 3)/(6 ÷ 3); x|= (5)/(2)]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution. Notice that the solution is a fraction. When solving multiplication equations, the answer may be a fraction, even if the initial equation only contains whole numbers.

Content:
Note: Dividing by the coefficient indeed removes it from the left-hand side. This is because dividing a product by a number is equivalent to dividing its coefficient:
[MATH: 6x \div 6 = (6 \div 6)x]

Content:
Recall that if the variable appears on the right-hand side (e.g., [MATH: 15=6x]), you may first swap the left and right sides of the equation to get [MATH: 6x=15.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: One-Step Multiplication Equations With Rational Coefficients

Content:
Sometimes, the coefficient of the variable in a multiplication equation is a fraction, such as in the equation

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}x=2.]

Content:
To isolate [MATH: x,] we need to undo multiplication by [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}.] We could do this by dividing both sides by [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}] as before.

Content:
However, dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. So, to solve a multiplication equation with a rational coefficient, we multiply both sides by the reciprocal of the coefficient.

Content:
In our case, the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{4}{5}] is [MATH: \dfrac{5}{4}.] We multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: \dfrac{5}{4}] and simplify.

Content:
On the left-hand side, we can re-group the numbers to multiply the fractions first. On the right-hand side, we can multiply fractions by first swapping denominators:

Content:
[MATH: (4)/(5)x|= 2; (4)/(5)x × (5)/(4)|= 2 × (5)/(4); ((4)/(5) × (5)/(4))x|= (2)/(4) × (5)/(1); 1x|= (1)/(2) × (5)/(1); x|= (5)/(2)]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution.
